items.stem: An engineer needs read-only access to logs in one project and nothing else. Which approach follows least privilege?

options.text: Grant a predefined role like Logs Viewer on that project
options.rationale: Correct: a predefined role scoped to the project grants only the needed read access.

options.text: Grant the Editor role at the organization level
options.rationale: Editor is broad and organization scope is far wider than one project.
Owner allows managing access and far exceeds read-only.

options.text: Add the user to a group with the Security Admin role
options.rationale: Security Admin manages security resources, not read-only log access.

items.explanation: Correct: Grant a predefined role like Logs Viewer on that project.

items.stem: Which TWO keep traffic to Google Cloud APIs off the public internet? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Enable Private Google Access on the subnet
options.rationale: Correct: Private Google Access lets instances without external IPs reach Google APIs privately.

options.text: Use VPC Service Controls / private endpoints
options.rationale: Correct: a service perimeter and private endpoints keep API traffic within a private boundary.

options.text: Assign every VM a public external IP
options.rationale: Public IPs push traffic over the internet, the opposite of the goal.
A default-allow rule broadens exposure and does not make API access private.

items.explanation: Correct: Enable Private Google Access on the subnet, Use VPC Service Controls / private endpoints.

items.stem: By default, which audit logs record who modified an IAM policy on a resource?

options.rationale: Correct: Admin Activity logs capture configuration changes such as IAM edits and are on by default.
Data Access logs record data reads/writes and are mostly off by default.
Flow Logs capture network traffic metadata, not IAM changes.
Billing export covers cost data, not IAM changes.
